description: Decision trees for RAG chatbot logic and medication interaction safety protocols

decision_trees.title: Can I Take HRT? Decision Tree
decision_trees.description: Step-by-step logic for determining HRT eligibility
decision_trees.purpose: Guide users through HRT eligibility assessment while emphasizing doctor consultation

steps.question: Symptom Severity Check
steps.ask_user: How would you describe your symptom severity: mild, moderate, or severe?

logic.mild: Suggest lifestyle changes first, mention HRT available if symptoms worsen

steps.question: Uterus Check (CRITICAL)
steps.ask_user: Do you still have a uterus? (Have you had a hysterectomy?)

logic.yes_have_uterus: Estrogen MUST be paired with progesterone to protect uterine lining
logic.no_uterus: Estrogen-only may be possible (safer for breast cancer risk)

steps.critical_note: This determines whether progesterone is needed

steps.question: Contraindication Screen
steps.ask_user: Do you have any of these conditions? (Answer yes/no to each)
conditions_to_screen: History of stroke or heart attack?
Current or past estrogen-sensitive cancer (breast, endometrial)?

logic.any_yes: ❌ Systemic HRT not recommended. Jump to Non-Hormonal Path. Note: Local vaginal estrogen may still be possible - discuss with doctor.

steps.question: Risk Context Assessment
steps.ask_user: To help assess your individual risk:
questions: How many years since your last period (if applicable)?
Do you have migraines with aura?

logic.low_risk: Age <60 AND <10 years since menopause AND non-smoker
logic.moderate_risk: Age 60+ OR >10 years since menopause OR smoker OR migraines with aura
logic.formulation_guidance: Transdermal estrogen (patch/gel) safer than oral, especially for blood clot risk and migraines

steps.question: Recommendation Output
steps.bot_response_template: Based on what you've shared, [ELIGIBILITY STATUS]. [FORMULATION RECOMMENDATION]. However, this is general information - a healthcare provider should assess your individual situation, medical history, and preferences to determine the best approach for you.

eligibility_statuses.likely_candidate: HRT may be a good option for you
eligibility_statuses.possible_with_caution: HRT may be possible but requires careful risk assessment
eligibility_statuses.not_recommended: Systemic HRT is not recommended due to contraindications, but non-hormonal options are available

formulation_recommendations.standard: Transdermal estrogen (patch or gel) with progesterone (if you have uterus) is often the preferred approach
formulation_recommendations.oral_ok: Oral or transdermal estrogen are both options
formulation_recommendations.transdermal_preferred: Transdermal estrogen is preferred over oral in your situation
formulation_recommendations.vaginal_only: Local vaginal estrogen may be appropriate for vaginal symptoms

critical_disclaimers: Always end with: 'Please discuss with a healthcare provider for personalized assessment'
Never give definitive yes/no - use 'may be an option' language

decision_trees.title: Non-Hormonal Management Path
decision_trees.description: Decision tree for non-hormonal treatment options

primary_symptom_assessment.question: What is your primary symptom concern?

hot_flashes.fda_approved: Fezolinetant (Veozah) - targets brain temperature regulation, 50-60% reduction
hot_flashes.lifestyle: Cooling strategies, trigger avoidance, stress management

sleep_insomnia.behavioral: CBT-I (Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia) - highly effective
sleep_insomnia.lifestyle: Sleep hygiene, cool bedroom, avoid caffeine/alcohol

mood_anxiety.medication: SSRIs if clinical depression (discuss with doctor)

vaginal_dryness.note: Vaginal estrogen may be possible even with cancer history - discuss with oncologist
vaginal_dryness.lifestyle: Regular use of moisturizers, lubricants for sex, adequate hydration

decision_trees.bot_safety_rule: Never stack multiple medications in one suggestion. Present options and emphasize doctor consultation for prescriptions.

decision_trees.title: Brain Fog & Cognitive Symptoms Decision Tree
decision_trees.description: Systematic approach to brain fog management

steps.question: Rule Out Sleep Issues
steps.ask_user: Are you sleeping less than 6 hours per night? Are you waking due to night sweats?

logic.yes_sleep_issues: Treat sleep first - poor sleep is major cause of brain fog. See sleep management strategies.

steps.question: Medication Review
steps.ask_user: Are you taking any of these medications?
flag_medications: Sleep aids (Ambien, etc.) - can cause next-day fog
Regular alcohol use - disrupts sleep and cognition
steps.logic: If yes to any, suggest discussing alternatives with doctor

options.forgetting_what: Forgetting names, words, where you put things (typical brain fog)
options.forgetting_how: Forgetting HOW to do familiar tasks (driving to familiar place, using appliances)

logic.forgetting_what: This is typical menopause brain fog. Provide coping strategies.
logic.forgetting_how: ⚠️ This requires medical evaluation - may be more than brain fog. Please see doctor within a week.

steps.question: Safe Coping Strategies
recommendations: External brain: Write everything down, use calendar reminders, task apps
Pace method: Schedule demanding tasks in morning
Meeting support: Request agendas, take notes, record when allowed
Reduce multitasking: Focus on one thing at a time
steps.treatment_options: HRT often improves brain fog for many women. Discuss with doctor.
steps.bot_rule: Do NOT suggest stimulants, nootropics, or unproven supplements

decision_trees.title: Vaginal/Sexual Symptoms Decision Tree
decision_trees.description: Pathway for vaginal dryness, pain, and sexual health

steps.question: Cancer History Check (CRITICAL)
steps.ask_user: Do you have a history of estrogen-sensitive cancer (breast, endometrial)?

logic.yes_cancer_history: ❌ Do not automatically recommend vaginal estrogen. Suggest: non-hormonal moisturizers, lubricants, pelvic PT. Note: Vaginal estrogen may be possible after oncologist approval.
logic.no_cancer_history: Vaginal estrogen is safe and highly effective. Also recommend moisturizers and lubricants.

dryness_pain.most_effective: Vaginal estrogen (cream, tablet, or ring) - 80-90% improvement
dryness_pain.non_hormonal: Hyaluronic acid moisturizers, regular use (not just before sex)
dryness_pain.lifestyle: Regular sexual activity (helps maintain tissue health), adequate hydration

recurrent_utis.explanation: Low estrogen thins bladder lining - this is Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause (GSM), not just hygiene
recurrent_utis.treatment: Vaginal estrogen can prevent recurrent UTIs
recurrent_utis.note: See doctor to rule out other causes

low_libido.hormonal: May be due to low testosterone or estrogen - discuss HRT with doctor
low_libido.psychological: Stress, relationship issues, body image - therapy may help
low_libido.physical: Pain during sex reduces desire - treat dryness first
low_libido.multifactorial: Often combination of factors - comprehensive approach needed

decision_trees.critical_note: Vaginal estrogen has very low systemic absorption and is safe for long-term use in most women

absolute_contraindications: History of stroke or heart attack
Current or recent estrogen-sensitive cancer (breast, endometrial)
relative_contraindications: Migraines with aura (transdermal safer than oral)
Strong family history of breast cancer (needs assessment)
hrt_contraindications.note: Local vaginal estrogen may be safe even with some contraindications - doctor decision

st_johns_wort.interaction: Reduces estrogen effectiveness by increasing metabolism
st_johns_wort.recommendation: Avoid while on HRT or use alternative for mood (discuss with doctor)
st_johns_wort.bot_warning: ⚠️ St. John's Wort can reduce hormone effectiveness and worsen symptoms. Please discuss with your doctor before combining.

vitamin_c_b6.interaction: High doses can interfere with estrogen metabolism
vitamin_c_b6.recommendation: Avoid very high supplemental doses (normal dietary intake is fine)
vitamin_c_b6.bot_warning: High doses of vitamin C and B6 may interfere with estrogen metabolism. Avoid mega-doses while on HRT.

black_cohosh.concern: Rare liver toxicity with long-term use
black_cohosh.recommendation: Monitor liver function if using long-term
black_cohosh.bot_warning: Black cohosh has rare liver risks. Please use caution and inform your doctor.

multiple_supplements.concern: Increased risk of interactions and side effects
multiple_supplements.recommendation: Less is more - focus on evidence-based supplements only
multiple_supplements.bot_warning: ⚠️ Combining multiple supplements can increase side effects. Stick to evidence-based options and inform your doctor of everything you take.

progesterone.reason: Often causes drowsiness - use this to help sleep
progesterone.benefit: Improves sleep quality, reduces daytime grogginess

estrogen_gel_patch.note: Gel must dry before contact with others (especially children/pets)

general_rule.principle: Start one new treatment at a time
general_rule.reason: Allows you to identify what helps and what causes side effects
general_rule.bot_rule: Never suggest starting multiple new medications/supplements simultaneously
